{"answer":"13","solution":"For a sorted solution, replace c by c′ = 3ab − c = (a² + b²)/c. This gives another positive integer solution. If b > 1, the quadratic f(x) = x² − 3abx + a² + b² has f(b) = a² − (3a − 2)b² < 0, so its roots satisfy c′ < b < c. Thus repeated replacement strictly decreases the largest entry. When b = 1, the only solutions are (1,1,1) and (1,1,2), giving the starting point for the descent.

Reversing the descent and retaining triples with largest entry at most 1000 gives exactly:
(1,1,1), (1,1,2), (1,2,5), (1,5,13), (1,13,34), (1,34,89), (1,89,233), (1,233,610), (5,13,194), (2,5,29), (2,29,169), (2,169,985), and (5,29,433).

At each listed triple, the reverse moves are obtained by replacing either of the two smaller entries with its other quadratic root. Applying both moves produces only triples in the list or triples whose largest entry exceeds 1000. Since every other solution descends to the starting point, the enumeration is complete.","insight":"Replacing c by 3ab − c preserves the equation and produces a positive integer.","insight_justification":"The equation is quadratic in c, with roots c and 3ab − c. Their product is a² + b² > 0, so the other root is positive; it is integral because a, b, and c are integers."}
